summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for hyponatremia and nausea. She had been drinking excess water due to fear of kidney failure, leading to polydipsia and low sodium. Fluid restriction improved her sodium levels, and she was restarted on torsemide for volume overload. She experienced an episode of chest pain, prompting cardiac testing that showed reduced ejection fraction on nuclear stress test; carvedilol was increased and imdur started. Hypertension and hyperkalemia led to dose adjustments in irbesartan. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions on fluid limits, daily weights, and cardiology follow-up.
